answer: Cross-Epoch Reputation Anchoring. Each identity accrues a rolling behavioural fingerprint across epochs; a new epoch’s actions must fall within a tolerance band of its prior history, or the identity enters a quarantine haven where its throughput is throttled until consistency recovers. Attackers must sustain coherent behaviour across many epochs, not just an initial island of activity. Rotating to fresh identities forfeits the accumulated fingerprint, so each replacement pays the full saffron cost of rebuilding trust from zero, making mass duplication economically draining.
